subject: Re: Mutual action plan + sequencing for MSA / DPA / Order Form
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@novacore.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novacore.io
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP + sequencing question for MSA/DPA/order form

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

Thanks again for last week's technical demo — the team was very impressed with the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to pull together a quick plan for legal sequencing so they can align internal reviewers. A few constraints from our side:

- Procurement wants the DPA signed before our security committee signs off on production access (they're stricter than usual).
- Legal prefers redlines to MSA in a single pass, but procurement is open to parallel review if we can guarantee consistent terms.
- Pricing and internal budget approval won't be final for another 3 weeks; order form signature may need to wait until then.

I've attached our evaluation plan and a short procurement checklist. Can you share a recommended MAP and a suggested order of operations? Specifically: should we aim to finish MSA first, DPA first, or run DPA and tech-eval in parallel and hold the order form until budget locks?

Appreciate a short proposed timeline (2–4 bullets) we can send upstream.

Cheers,
Elena
Elena Martin
Director, Strategic Sourcing | Novacore
[Attachment: Novacore_EvalPlan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@novacore.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + sequencing question for MSA/DPA/order form

Elena — thanks for the clear constraints and the eval plan. High level recommendation (short):

1) Parallelize DPA review + technical evaluation: start DPA redline review immediately and run security evidence collection in parallel with the tech eval. That keeps the critical-path items moving without blocking signing.
2) Finalize MSA terms in a single negotiated pass (legal prefers this): propose a one-week internal review, then a single redline exchange week.
3) Order form (pricing) can be held until budget sign-off, but lock in negotiated commercial terms in the MAP so the signatures are just administrative once budget is approved.

Proposed MAP milestones (dates are placeholders until Novacore confirms budget):
- Day 0 (today): Kickoff — share Novacore eval plan and Redwood MAP draft.
- Day 3–10: DPA redline cycle + security evidence (SOC2 reports, retention controls) — procurement and security reviewers parallel.
- Day 10–17: MSA redline cycle (single pass), finalize legal exhibits.
- Day 17–21+: Order form sign after pricing approval; DocuSign execution.

I'll attach a short MAP PDF (draft) that lays this out and call out owners. Two asks for you:
- Can procurement confirm whether DPA signature before production access is a hard block (i.e., no sandbox provisioning until DPA signed)?
- Who owns pricing sign-off (title/name/email) so we can call them out in the MAP?

Attaching: Redwood_MAP_proposal.pdf (draft).

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of GTM Ops | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_MAP_proposal.pdf (PDF)]

From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@novacore.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novacore.io
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: MAP + sequencing question for MSA/DPA/order form

Sofia — thanks, that sequencing makes sense. Quick clarifications from procurement/security:

- The DPA-before-production rule is a hard requirement from our Data Governance Office for any vendor that will process PHI/PII. We can, however, permit limited sandbox access to non-production data if your infra team signs a short tech attestation (we would need evidence logs).
- Pricing sign-off: Budget owner will be Olivia Chen (olivia.chen@novacore.io), VP Product Ops — procurement will route the final order form to her once legal clears the commercial terms.
- Suggested parallel tasks we want you to run ASAP: provide a DPA checklist (mapping of clauses we typically need: data residency, subprocessor list, breach notification SLA), and an evidence package (SOC2 + data retention matrix).

I've attached our redline to your standard DPA to speed things up — it's not final but shows the blocking edits. Procurement copied.

If you're OK, let's lock the timeline like this:
- Week 0: Kickoff + Redwood sends DPA checklist + evidence package.
- Week 0–1: Novacore and Redwood exchange DPA redlines (procurement + legal).
- Week 1–2: MSA single-pass redline (legal).
- Week 2: Order form prepared and routed to Olivia once pricing is confirmed.

This still allows technical evaluation to proceed in parallel (we want to avoid waiting on order form).

Best,
Elena
[Attachment: DPA_redline_from_Novacore.pdf (PDF)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@novacore.io>, procurement@novacore.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 15:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: MAP + sequencing question for MSA/DPA/order form

Elena / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the DPA redline. Confirming we will proceed with the parallel path you outlined. Short mutual action plan (owners & near-term asks):

- Redwood (Sofia / Karthik): share DPA checklist + SOC2 + retention matrix by EOD Monday (owner: karthik_iyer@redwood.com).
- Novacore (Elena / procurement): circulate internal DPA redline to legal and confirm whether sandbox attestation will allow limited test access (owner: procurement@novacore.io).
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare an MSA redline-ready package and proposed exhibit language for order form pricing anchoring (owner: marissa_cole@redwood.com).
- Novacore (Olivia): pricing approval / budget confirmation expected within 3 weeks — procurement to notify when locked.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: If DPA takes >2 redline cycles, production access will be delayed. Mitigation: we will provide stronger evidence upfront (logs + attestation) to shorten cycles.
- Risk: Order form signature waits on budget. Mitigation: lock commercial terms in the MAP so DocuSign execution is administrative.

Next steps: I'll send the DPA checklist + evidence package first thing Monday, and Marissa will push the MSA prep. If procurement confirms sandbox attestation, we can provision a limited test seat for two engineers within 48 hours.

If that all looks good, I'll convert this thread into a shared MAP doc (Drive link) and include the agreed owners and dates.

Thanks — talk Monday.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Head of GTM Ops | Redwood Inference
S: +1 415 555 0198
